Senses.Explanation: The stock pair “exposed pillar and lantern” (露柱燈籠) names two monastery fixtures that Chan hall sayings repeatedly make speak, laugh, nod, celebrate, or stand vividly alive. Daosheng says that when restraint is released the pillar and lantern are “lively and leaping” (活鱍鱍); another address says they “blazingly preach” (熾然說), while others have them laugh and nod or celebrate a buddha-day. These personified actions are corpus facts: the pair names ordinary fixtures granted speaking and acting roles by the records.
